# Modified OpenHMD acquisition engine

Source: [Jan Schmidt's OpenHMD fork](https://github.com/thaytan/OpenHMD), branch `rift-kalman-filter`, commit [`a4ebf094e8be5c53c43c5f68d92e87afa5bdf0c8`](https://github.com/thaytan/OpenHMD/commit/a4ebf094e8be5c53c43c5f68d92e87afa5bdf0c8), dated 2026-07-29 ("rift: Backport pose metric tweaks from Monado"). Imported as source, without upstream history; this is a modified snapshot, not an unmodified upstream release.

Most source is under Boost Software License 1.0; dual-license files are used under their Boost option. `nxjson` retains MIT, and `miniz` retains Unlicense/public-domain terms. See the individual source headers, this directory's `LICENSE`, and the root `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`. The unused upstream GStreamer plugin and 3Glasses driver are omitted; other upstream hardware sources are retained but only the Rift driver is configured by cv1touch.

Local changes expose a bounded CV1 acquisition API, controller/radio decoding, factory geometry, timestamps, raw/labelled observations, optional PipeWire views, fixed calibrated camera poses, radio-only headset operation, and more resilient camera transfers. Tracking for cv1touch is performed in Rust. Native dependencies are resolved from the system; OpenCV 4 and 5 discovery is supported. The small nxjson UTF-8 encoder is replaced with an independently written Unicode-scalar encoder and boundary tests.

Compare this snapshot against the pinned upstream commit to inspect the complete modification set. Subsequent release changes are tracked in this repository. Preserve upstream notices when modifying or extracting code.

The UVC stream stop flag is atomic, and tracker teardown signals every stream before changing any USB alternate setting or waiting for transfers. Completion callbacks park failed submissions and return immediately; engine updates retry parked transfers at most once per 10 ms, including when no transfers remain in flight. This prevents a peer's retry loop from blocking shutdown or startup-failure cleanup while retaining recovery from transient submission errors. `test_uvc_shutdown` exercises peer shutdown, bounded retries, recovery, and frame lifetime without devices.

The CV1 extension exposes a controller's cached factory-calibration identity for binding optional user input calibration to that controller. The identity is copied when factory calibration completes; controller sample and shared-memory layouts are unchanged. Factory-normalized analog values remain unbounded at acquisition so the input-calibration guide can measure shifted endpoints; the Rust daemon applies user correction and bounds values before SteamVR publication.

Sensor discovery now owns a dynamically sized registry, and an additional configuration setter deep-copies complete ignore/pose lists without changing the existing scalar configuration ABI. Discovery rejects unusable/duplicate identities and cleans up failed starts. Constructors unwind partial allocations, and shutdown retains frame storage until analysis workers have joined. The unused fixed-size pose report array is replaced with a used-observation flag. Native tests cover discovery/configuration through 65 synthetic sensors, allocation failures, and outstanding-frame lifetime; practical USB/resource limits remain.

The engine's log goes to its C runtime's stdout. `ohmd_cv1touch_unbuffer_log` turns that stream's buffering off; on Windows the library carries its own C runtime, whose stdout is fully buffered when it is a pipe or a file, so the daemon calls it there.

`src/drv_oculus_rift/rift-sensor-blobwatch.c` uses an empty extent range on the first processed scanline without accessing a null previous line. The Linux native `blobwatch_ubsan` regression compiles blob extraction with UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer and recovery disabled; it covers dark and lit first scanlines, following extents, the last scanline, and repeated frames with both scalar and SIMD scanning.

UVC capture rejects incomplete raw images and damaged header/FID/PTS sequences before delivering a frame. Complete raw images are still delivered on the packet supplying their last byte, without waiting for EOF. After a delivered image, damage before the next boundary costs nothing, a new PTS starts the next image even if FID repeats, and only extra raw payload discards the following image. Before the first boundary after a stream starts, a header with a new presentation time also starts an image when the frame ID is unchanged, provided both headers carried a presentation time. The first packet after a stream opens is left over from an earlier stream: its timestamp predates this stream's clock. That clock restarts when the stream starts and runs at about 40 MHz. The first image arrives about 1 s later with frame ID 0 and a new timestamp. When the leftover also had frame ID 0, that image was rejected as out of sequence: on three five-sensor starts, four, four and two sensors, 145 to 157 packets each. An opening header without a presentation time does not start that image. A frame-ID change with the same presentation time remains a sequence error, including before that boundary. The opening packet's error flag is treated as before. JPEG images are delivered at a packet-ending outer EOI after SOS, or at EOF. Before SOS, the assembler skips marker payloads by their lengths so an APP thumbnail cannot end the main image. A structurally valid header establishes its frame boundary before its error flag is applied. Rejected candidates retain their assembler-owned buffer until reuse or teardown. Analysis also validates the exact packed GRAY8 layout. JPEG decoding rejects the libjpeg warnings that mean concealed damage (`JWRN_JPEG_EOF`, `JWRN_HIT_MARKER`, `JWRN_HUFF_BAD_CODE`, `JWRN_ARITH_BAD_CODE`, `JWRN_MUST_RESYNC`, `JWRN_BOGUS_PROGRESSION`, and `JWRN_EXTRANEOUS_DATA` before any marker but EOI) and keeps images with any other warning. The per-event UVC and JPEG messages are replaced by per-sensor summaries of discarded images by reason, at most one line every 10 s from the assembler and one from the decoder; malformed packets and repeated raw overruns continue to advance the reporting window without counting each packet as another image, and the buffer-starvation warning pair is unchanged. These checks remain partial: libjpeg-turbo can decode damaged entropy without a concealment warning, even through its slow Huffman path. Native fixtures exercise the real assembler, reused stale pixels through blob extraction, decoder recovery, the capture callback guard, log rate limits and frame ownership without opening devices.

A separate 56-byte sensor-video quality getter reports negotiated raw/JPEG input, accepted JPEG decodes and rejected image candidates, leaving the 40-byte acquisition record unchanged. Raw capture validates layout before advancing acquisition, still before any analysis lock. JPEG progress advances only after decoding and exact GRAY8 layout validation. Assembly and validation share a device-owned, relaxed-atomic rejected-candidate counter; malformed packets without an image, buffer starvation and intentional queue evictions are excluded. Neither counter reporting nor the getter waits for frame boundaries or changes exposure timing.

Label inspection keeps the calibrated camera pose for fast tracking, and overrides the long-search skip mask only for the requested controller IDs. Each inspected hand has one private candidate track, seeded by a cold correspondence and followed at camera rate. Its copied labels and camera transform cannot enter shared blobwatch, trusted fast priors or exported poses until motion establishes identity. A candidate that fails the motion check is discarded so it cannot monopolise the inspection. None of this adds radio-thread work or runs outside inspections.

Identity belongs to a continuous correspondence. At least five unchanged raw-blob/LED pairs must survive consecutive frames, with no raw-frame gap over 60 ms. Every pair also needs an inspection-local image lineage whose displacement stays within 32 px on every raw frame, including intervening frames without a pose. Across ten captures, 3,162,942 inherited pairs retaining the same recorded LED label had median/p95/p99 displacements of 0.156/6.458/13.459 px; 99.836% stayed within 32 px. Those labels are not independent physical truth, and the 1120.882 px maximum includes erroneous associations. Blobwatch itself is unchanged. A jump resets the private lineage even if blobwatch copies the same software ID. Delayed label updates are filtered against the live lineage before shared labels or priors can be installed. Across ten recordings, 480,145 intervals had a 22.14 ms 99.9th percentile and a 41.05 ms maximum. A lost correspondence or gap resets the anchor, agreement count and latch; cold reacquisition must validate again. An alternative fit cannot replace an intact trusted stream merely by changing its LED assignments. Empty observations advance the frame epoch without entering pose helpers that require blobs.

Before exporting labels, the candidate's camera-relative rotation must follow that hand's IMU across at least thirty degrees and three agreeing exposures within three seconds, with angular error at most ten percent of the turn. If the other controller has IMU data, its turn angle must differ by at least half the requested hand's turn. This rejects a fixed alias of the other hand only while both endpoints belong to the same continuous correspondence. It does not depend on the disputed camera rotation. Static, slow and indistinguishable two-hand motion cannot establish identity. A swap during an image overlap is caught only once the hands' rotations diverge; identical motion through an overlap can preserve the swapped stream. The crossing regression retains it for four seconds of identical rotation, and there is no fixed lifetime until the motions differ. The geometric-certificate follow-up in `docs/inspection-identity-recovery.md` addresses physical provenance.

A continuous validated identity survives stillness, a slow turn or a return toward its anchor. Three consecutive tracked exposures disagreeing with its IMU by more than ten degrees, or a tenth of the turn when larger, revoke it. A single rejected output preserves the live labels that the next raw frame needs; it cannot export them or become a new anchor. A cold alternative while the original tracks remain is rejected without replacing them. Each identity check consumes its exposure, avoiding a redundant cold search of the same pending fast match. Motion flags distinguish an inspection starved by still hands from one that found no agreement. Extending an active inspection into placement retains its continuous tracks after cancelling the old search and draining queued frames; restoration or expiry resets them.

Inspection evidence has a separate monotonically increasing 64-bit identity epoch, captured on each accepted frame. The former reserved words carry that tag without changing the frame layout. An additive callback reports Started, Ended and Invalidated under the sensor lock. A normal loss of continuity or restoration ends future permission without discrediting earlier checks; a contradiction retrospectively invalidates the epoch. Rust keeps only the invalidations, coalesced outside its dropping camera queue, and rejects delayed invalidated frames until the restored pose is acknowledged, by which time every tagged frame has been delivered. The recorder preserves them as additive v2 type 9 events. During an inspection, eighty eligible observed checks across at least two windows, with the unchanged sixty-percent miss threshold, can establish movement; invalidation retracts the epoch's checks and window contributions. The lifecycle harness exercises both reasons and releases an older frame after a newer epoch ended to verify its full-width captured tag.

At the fast-to-long handoff, the long worker receives a detached observation. It queues copied label updates under the sensor lock; only the fast worker applies them to blobwatch and installs a private camera prior between frames. A contradicted identity or restoration revokes those labels and that prior. An older cold result remains unknown and cannot revoke newer validated labels or priors, and labels the fast worker installs directly supersede anything still queued for that controller. Revocation preserves another controller's current label when only its previous label belonged to the inspected hand. The calibrated pose stays fixed, and inspected controller poses never update native fusion through the disputed calibration. A successful identity is marked in the additive CV1 extension match flags, so Rust can judge the sensor while retaining its absolute attitude guard for fusion. An early search callback lets the Rust consumer retain the exposure's prior until completion or cancellation.

Runtime pose restoration and sensor shutdown cooperatively cancel correspondence searches at their loop boundaries. Label inspections also have a native monotonic deadline. The CV1 extension reports when the queued pose is applied and the preceding search has stopped and its queued frames are released; the daemon retains its inspection slot until that acknowledgement. `test_search_cancel` parks a real search loop while restoring its pose or expiring its deadline and checks cancellation, queued-work invalidation and delayed acknowledgement without devices. It also wakes the other controller while the real search loop is blocked, in both hand orders. `test_search_skip` checks hand isolation. `test_inspection_tracking` uses actual correspondence search and OpenCV PnP with fictional geometry: one cold candidate followed by independent motion establishes identity and feeds a hundred fresh, unlabelled fast frames at camera rotations from five to forty-five degrees. Through the same search, an exact alias of the other hand at a fixed 120-degree offset, turned in step with the requested hand's IMU, and a rigid turn about that offset's axis stay unknown; an unmoved sensor's still hand never queues a cold search; and a trial costs a single stop poll. `test_inspection_handoff` checks mirrored and rigid two-hand ambiguity, each bound of the discrimination clause, a missing other hand, the kept identity through stillness past the first anchor, a return toward it, PnP noise on a still hand, outliers that neither revoke nor become the anchor, a sustained alias swap, repeated cold aliases, the exported motion flags, documented slow turns and wiggles, rejection and restoration in both hand orders, a genuine-to-alias reacquisition before and after validation, changed LED assignments, raw-frame gaps, an empty observation, private candidate isolation and rejection, placement handoff and expiry, large physical-source migrations with unchanged software IDs before and after validation, jumps between judged frames, private-candidate jumps, delayed label transfer across a jump, one-pixel overlaps with divergent and identical rotations, live-label propagation after an outlier, observation ownership, queued labels superseded by newer fast labels, and real concurrent label production and fast-worker transfer. Its interleaving also passes under ThreadSanitizer on Linux.

The Linux Rust pipeline regression consumes the native crossing test's actual flags and label counts and projects observations against fresh peer updates. The crossing supplies one ambiguous labelled check before three rejected exposures; it causes no movement verdict or placement probe. This covers an inspection before demotion, not an already-running placement or indefinitely identical motion.
